_comment: Course de-duplication for brevity/simplicity of the experience. Each group collapses title-and-scope near-duplicate MIT courses WITHIN one level into a single representative node, keeping one member's id (so preselects and edges survive), a representative title, the union of edges, and ALL members' catalog evidence. Applied deterministically by scripts/assemble-dataset.mjs (mergeCourses); provenance is preserved in the dataset's mergedFrom / meta.flags.mergedCourses. Authored by domain judgment for the live Data tab; the ground-catalog workflow's Simplify phase produces this file for future runs.

merges.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
merges.rationale: Five level-1000 introductions to probability/statistics (Intro to Probability, Intro to Statistical Methods in Economics, Applied Probability and Statistics, Intro to Probability and Statistics, Probability and Random Variables) are interchangeable foundational options; collapse to one intro-stats node.

merges.title: Linear Algebra
merges.rationale: Linear Algebra and Linear Algebra and Optimization are the same foundational linear-algebra course family at level 1000.

merges.title: Fundamentals of Statistics
merges.rationale: Three level-2000 statistics/data-analysis courses (Fundamentals of Statistics, Introduction to Statistical Data Analysis, Statistical Thinking and Data Analysis) cover the same intermediate statistics ground.

merges.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
merges.rationale: Introduction to Machine Learning and Modeling with Machine Learning for Computer Science are the same level-3000 ML course.

merges.title: Optimization Methods
merges.rationale: Optimization Methods and Optimization Methods in Business Analytics are the same level-3000 optimization course.
